items.title: NEWS: Senators Blunt Rochester, Curtis Introduce Bills to Help Public Understand Impacts of Data Centers
items.summary: Release describing the Senate transparency bill (EPA and EIA collection) and a community technical-assistance bill.

quote.text: The answer to that distrust is transparency.
quote.speaker: Sen. John Curtis

items.author: Joshua Siegel
items.title: New in @PunchbowlNews: What's next for permitting
items.summary: Siegel posts his Punchbowl News item on what comes next. Utilities may push to weaken the expanded FERC backstop siting authority and the mandatory data center cost language, which the item calls stronger than the voluntary Ratepayer Protection Act that Senate Democrats blocked. Environmental groups are expected to contest the limits on NEPA remedies and the Clean Water Act section 401 changes, and Rep. Jared Huffman said progressives may hold out for more next Congress.

quote.text: Negotiators say they struck a difficult balance that'll be hard to defeat. But landmines are here.
quote.speaker: Joshua Siegel

items.author: Shanu Mathew
items.title: Senate’s permitting deal could make power infrastructure easier to finance while requiring data centers to commit more capital to secure electricity.
items.summary: Mathew, an investor and portfolio manager who writes on energy and infrastructure, lists five terms: the 150-day NEPA challenge window, FERC backstop siting with beneficiary-pays cost allocation, the end of the federal right of first refusal, limits on permit revocation with damages, and data center cost responsibility. His data center description matches the text: loads of 20 MW or more bear incremental generation, storage and grid costs, with financial assurance before construction and recovery continuing if the load exits (section 2107, new FPA section 228).

quote.text: Senate’s permitting deal could make power infrastructure easier to finance while requiring data centers to commit more capital to secure electricity.
quote.speaker: Shanu Mathew

visuals.title: Permitting and transmission
visuals.text: Six terms (the 150-day challenge window, remand without vacatur, permit durability, FERC backstop siting, beneficiary pays and the right-of-first-refusal ban), each with what the bill does and why it matters for project risk.

visuals.title: Data-center power commitments
visuals.text: Five terms from section 2107 (the 20 MW threshold, incremental costs, financial assurance, exit liability and existing agreements), showing who pays and when.

items.author: Jane Flegal
items.title: The data center language in the permitting deal is the best yet
items.summary: Flegal says the bill makes data centers pay both the full cost of the upgrades they cause and a share of the existing grid. Section 2107 does both for transmission: FERC must charge these loads embedded plus incremental cost, and new Federal Power Act section 228 keeps incremental costs off other customers. Her estimate of billions of dollars a year for ratepayers is her own; the bill gives no figure.

quote.text: forces data centers to pay full costs they cause AND their share of the existing grid.
quote.speaker: Jane Flegal

items.author: Christopher Barnard
items.title: Really positive & good faith statement on permitting reform out of the White House Office of Public Liaison
items.summary: Barnard posts a screenshot of a White House Office of Public Liaison email saying the bill advances the President's agenda. The email lists permit certainty, judicial review changes and transmission permitting among its key provisions. Its claim that issued permits are protected from being overturned is broader than section 1401, which restrains agencies but still lets a court order a revocation.

items.author: Aidan Mackenzie
items.title: So how will the permitting reform deal (BAAJA) get big transmission lines built?
items.summary: Mackenzie, an infrastructure fellow at the Institute for Progress, explains how the bill would fix interregional transmission: neighboring regions must complete joint planning on a common set of benefits, FERC approves cost allocation for the lines they select, and FERC can site qualifying lines when states deny them without a designated corridor. These points match sections 2101 and 2103. His figures on Order 1000 projects and merchant lines are not sourced in the thread and are not checked against the bill.

quote.text: So how will the permitting reform deal (BAAJA) get big transmission lines built?
quote.speaker: Aidan Mackenzie

items.title: Senate permitting bill would expand federal role in transmission siting
items.summary: Reports on BAAJA expanding FERC authority to permit interstate transmission lines, eliminating NIETCs and the federal right of first refusal, with reactions from Rob Gramlich and Devin Hartman.

quote.text: The transmission title as well as the impact of the other sections on transmission development are very well-crafted.
quote.speaker: Rob Gramlich, Grid Strategies

items.author: Nico Portuondo
items.title: Senate bipartisan permitting deal faces a House buzz saw
items.summary: House Natural Resources ranking member Jared Huffman said most House Democrats will not support the Senate bill as written and urged talks to resume after the midterms. The report says Energy and Commerce Chair Brett Guthrie had not endorsed it.

quote.text: Folding our hand now or in the lame duck makes no sense when we can keep working on this and, in a few more months, have a much better deal that works for everyone.
quote.speaker: Rep. Jared Huffman (D-Calif.)

items.author: Robinson Meyer
items.title: The Senate Permitting Deal Contains a Data Center Double Tap
items.summary: Meyer explains the bill's ratepayer provisions for data centers and crypto miners. FERC would have to price transmission service for these customers at both embedded and incremental cost, a new Federal Power Act section would bar shifting incremental costs to other customers for loads of 20 megawatts or more, and states could set less favorable rates and run open seasons. The piece says the changes would apply to "future data centers" but does not state that section 228 covers only loads that interconnect after enactment and leaves existing arrangements in place.

quote.text: Call it the data center double tap.
quote.speaker: Robinson Meyer

items.author: Katie Brigham
items.title: The Climate Tech Winners and Losers of the Senate’s Permitting Bill
items.summary: Brigham sorts the bill's effects by climate tech sector and concludes most sectors gain. She names geothermal, grid-enhancing technologies, virtual power plants and critical minerals as winners, and says data center costs would shift from ratepayers to developers. The data center point is stated without noting that the ratepayer section applies only to loads that connect after enactment.

quote.text: The bill requires utilities to conduct recurring evaluations on technologies that could increase the capacity of existing transmission infrastructure
quote.speaker: Katie Brigham

items.author: Alexander C. Kaufman
items.title: The Permitting Reform Bill Just Dropped
items.summary: The morning newsletter's lead item reports the 417-page bill and links Heatmap's explainer. It says the bill would change how data centers are built and whether transmission lines get constructed, then focuses on passage odds: House Democrats are weighing whether to wait past the November election, and a Republican source says the House will not be called back to vote before it.

quote.text: Most Democrats will want to see how things go on Nov. 3 and then do a reality check
quote.speaker: Rep. Jared Huffman

items.author: Chirag Lala
items.title: The bipartisan permitting bill gets transmission right
items.summary: A brief on the bill's grid title. It says the bill goes further than the 2024 EPRA bill: FERC must permit qualifying interstate lines when a state has not approved them within a year, DOE-identified congested areas replace national interest corridors, and costs follow a beneficiary-pays rule. It also covers the data center cost rule, the right-of-first-refusal ban and advanced transmission technologies, and notes that DOE's transmission loan program needs new money because the One Big Beautiful Bill Act rescinded its funding.

quote.text: Most importantly, BAAJA gives FERC more statutory cover to take aggressive actions on grid development.
quote.speaker: Chirag Lala, Center for Public Enterprise

items.title: The Permitting Bill: Its Procedural Reforms, Explained
items.summary: Alex Mechanick analyzes BAAJA procedural overhaul, focusing on the end of project-stopping injunctions under NEPA and NHPA in favor of remand to correct errors while projects proceed.

quote.text: The most important reform in BAAJA is that violations of NEPA and NHPA can no longer be the basis for stopping a project. Instead, if a court finds a violation, it remands to the agency to correct the error
quote.speaker: Alex Mechanick

items.author: Ethan Howland
items.title: FERC chair slams PJM 'mess' as country's largest grid operator delays power auction
items.summary: Reports FERC's partial approval of PJM's reliability backstop and PJM's decision to delay its auction.

quote.text: This commission will not be forced into accepting a deeply flawed, eleventh-hour procurement mechanism with billion-dollar implications for consumers.
quote.speaker: FERC Chairman Laura Swett

items.title: Voluntary ratepayer protection bill blocked in Senate again
items.summary: Reports the 57-43 cloture failure, the four Democratic votes, Schumer's objection that the bill is voluntary, and that states need only start consideration within a year and finish within two.

quote.text: The bill would not require states to adopt any particular standard, only start the process to consider new rules within one year of its enactment and complete it within two.
quote.speaker: Roll Call

quote.speaker: Sen. Chuck Schumer

items.title: Senate Democrats sink 'toothless' stock trading ban, data center bill in last act before election recess

items.title: Lots of good in BAAJA, including shrinking our juristocracy & vetocracy

The wind point goes further than the text: the wind and solar side agreement is not in the bill, and section 1402 suits cannot be filed until 180 or 280 days after enactment.

quote.text: it'll re-empower elected officials to do things we elected them to do and save us money and jobs.

items.title: Lee, Capito, Heinrich, and Whitehouse Introduce Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026

items.author: Jane Flegal
items.title: The permitting bill is out and it’s awesome
items.summary: A 15-post thread. Flegal credits Whitehouse and Heinrich, calls the permit certainty sections a guard against future administrations, and praises the transmission title's regional and interregional planning, backstop siting and cost allocation rules. She cites C2ES and Greenline Insights modeling of 71 million fewer tons of CO2 in 2035 across the regions studied. Two posts go beyond the text: section 1401 pays delay costs plus 25 to 50 percent of costs incurred, not full reimbursement, and the new EIA reporting falls on utilities, not data centers.

items.author: Zeke Hausfather
items.title: Confused by all the debate about the new permitting reform bill?
items.summary: Hausfather, a climate scientist who writes The Climate Brink, posts a one-page table of the bill's main provisions grouped by whom they help, with his own estimate of each one's effect on emissions. Transmission, renewables and geothermal on public land, historic preservation and offshore wind leasing mostly help clean energy; NEPA deadlines and lawsuit limits, permit certainty and the discrimination damages cut both ways; pipeline, drilling and narrower NEPA scope changes mostly help fossil fuels. The section numbers match the text. His line that courts cannot cancel permits applies to NEPA claims (section 1110), and the emissions sizes are his judgment.

quote.text: Here is a quick cheat-sheet of the most important provisions, and their likely impact on emissions
quote.speaker: Zeke Hausfather

visuals.title: What's in the Senate permitting deal
visuals.text: Ten provisions sorted into mostly helps clean energy, cuts both ways and mostly helps fossil fuels, each with its section numbers and an emissions estimate from small to large.

items.author: Aidan Mackenzie

quote.text: Projects should not spend years or even decades navigating duplicative reviews and regulatory uncertainty before construction can begin.
quote.speaker: Ross Marchand, Taxpayers Protection Alliance

items.author: Rachel Frazin
items.title: Senators reach bipartisan deal on permitting reform
items.summary: Reports the four senators announced the deal and expect a lame-duck vote, that Whitehouse says wind and solar permitting under the Trump administration remains unresolved, and that a White House official expressed support.

quote.speaker: Sen. Shelley Moore Capito

items.title: Sierra Club Reaction to Permitting Bill Introduction
items.summary: Sierra Club notes the urgency of transmission and clean energy but raises concern over fossil fuel infrastructure acceleration without deployment guarantees.

quote.text: There is no task more urgent than building clean energy and transmission. Congress must act to lower energy bills, protect clean air and water, and transition off of fossil fuels, and that means making it faster and easier to build transmission and clean energy.
quote.speaker: Holly Bender, Sierra Club

items.author: POLITICO staff (Nico Portuondo and Pavan Acharya contributed)

The cloture vote failed 57-43; four Democrats joined all Republicans in favor.

quote.text: All the issues are solved in concept
quote.speaker: Sen. Angus King (I-Maine)

items.author: Manish Bapna
items.title: Permitting Bill: “Desperately Needed” But Must Improve

quote.text: The transmission provisions contained in the bill are desperately needed; the question is do those benefits outweigh the cost of the rollbacks to the foundational environmental laws of this country.
quote.speaker: Manish Bapna, NRDC President and CEO

items.author: Liza Reed
items.title: Niskanen Center supports introduction of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026
items.summary: Niskanen Center supports the bill and calls its transmission planning and siting provisions the most consequential congressional transmission policy in two decades.

quote.speaker: Liza Reed, Niskanen Center

items.title: Bipartisan Senate Deal Answers Manufacturers’ Call for Permitting Reform
items.summary: NAM welcomes the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 and says it answers the group's call for faster, more predictable federal reviews and NEPA reform.

quote.text: Comprehensive permitting reform will unleash growth and investment across the board.
quote.speaker: Jay Timmons, NAM President and CEO

items.title: LCV Statement on Senate Permitting Deal

quote.speaker: Sara Chieffo, LCV Senior Vice President of Government Affairs

items.author: Catherine Boudreau
items.title: Senators strike bipartisan permitting deal

items.author: Robinson Meyer
items.title: The Senate’s Big Bipartisan Permitting Deal, Explained
items.summary: Heatmap's guide to the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, which it says would remove longstanding roadblocks to expanding the power grid and developing new energy infrastructure.

quote.speaker: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse

items.author: Thomas Hochman
items.title: The Permitting Grand Bargain Is Here
items.summary: Hochman walks through each title of the bill and calls it more aggressive than he expected on both grid and conventional permitting reform. He highlights the 150-day NEPA limitations period, the end of injunctions and vacatur for NEPA-only claims, new revocation limits with damages, FERC backstop siting without a designated corridor, and the state referral power over local transmission spending. He expects Senate and House votes in the lame duck. His account of the NEPA remedies, revocation damages and FERC siting matches the text (sections 1110, 1401 and 2101).

quote.text: Third and most importantly, injunctions and vacatur are eliminated outright for NEPA-specific claims.
quote.speaker: Thomas Hochman

items.title: Senate unveils bipartisan deal tackling energy and data centers — but wind and solar questions remain
items.summary: Reports the 417-page bipartisan text, its permitting speedups and data center cost provisions, and that wind and solar language tied to the Trump administration remains unresolved.

quote.speaker: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse

quote.speaker: Heatmap AM

items.author: David Jordan and Kelly Livingston
items.title: Permitting bill off until after midterms even as talks close in
items.summary: Reports Whitehouse saying a vote will likely slip to the November lame-duck session and that negotiators were close to finalizing text.

quote.text: over the hump on the deal-break issues
quote.speaker: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse

items.author: POLITICO staff (Amelia Davidson contributed)
items.title: Permitting won't get vote ahead of election
items.summary: Senate negotiators did not close a deal that week, so a permitting vote would wait until after the elections. Democrats wanted more review time and firmer assurances that the administration would stop attacking clean energy projects. The story lists Section 401, NEPA limits and NHPA as likely parts of any package.

quote.text: we need just a bit more clarity on exactly what return to regular order for wind and solar projects looks like
quote.speaker: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.)

items.author: Austin Corona
items.title: Gas, solar, and tech companies all want this bill. Will Congress pass it?
items.summary: Reports that a bipartisan Senate group says it is close to a permitting deal, and that polling suggests tying reform to data centers is politically costly.

quote.text: If you phrase permitting reform as serving data centers, the polling results get way worse
quote.speaker: Alex Lundry, Redbud Consulting

items.author: Cami Mondeaux
items.title: Permitting reform talks fall apart in the Senate, deal punted until after midterms
items.summary: Reports Senate permitting negotiations stalled and a deal was pushed past the midterm elections; quotes Majority Whip Barrasso blaming Democrats. Article was updated Sept. 29.

quote.text: Republicans are 100% committed to permitting reform. The Democrats – specifically Chuck Schumer – don’t seem to care at all
quote.speaker: Sen. John Barrasso

items.author: Lisa Martine Jenkins and Catherine Boudreau
items.title: Exclusive: Heinrich proposes 30% credit for long-haul transmission
items.summary: Reports Heinrich introducing a bill for a 30% investment tax credit on long-haul transmission lines, as President Trump suggests he is willing to remove some barriers to permitting reform.

items.author: Josh Siegel
items.title: Trump will green-light wind energy projects to strike permitting deal
items.summary: Trump told advisers he would direct the Defense Department to start clearing its queue of delayed onshore wind projects to close a permitting deal. Thune had set a Tuesday deadline for a deal so a bill could move before senators left to campaign.

quote.text: President Donald Trump signaled he would ease his administration's blockade on renewable energy projects to entice Democrats to agree to a permitting deal.
quote.speaker: POLITICO Pro (Josh Siegel)

items.author: Matthew Zeitlin
items.title: What's a Utility to Do When Everyone Is Mad at Them?
items.summary: Industry insiders told Heatmap that utilities' political weakness is one reason a deal could pass, because interregional transmission reform could threaten utility spending in their own territories. EEI has backed permitting reform publicly since last year.

quote.text: They are gonna get smoked in the Senate permitting deal
quote.speaker: An energy industry figure following the negotiations, anonymous

items.author: Josiah Neeley
items.title: Low Energy Fridays: Permitting Reform Remains Close, But So Far
items.summary: R Street's Low-Energy Fridays newsletter on the state of permitting reform talks as Congress returned from the August recess.

items.author: Nico Portuondo, Amelia Davidson and Pavan Acharya
items.title: Senate roadblock sparks new competition over data center bills
items.summary: After Heinrich objected to Husted's unanimous-consent request on the Ratepayer Protection Act, Blumenthal and Hawley pitched their GRID Act in a letter to Energy and Natural Resources leaders. The story frames the House-passed bill as stalled in the Senate.

quote.text: those hopes were dashed Thursday after Sen. Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.) objected to Sen. Jon Husted’s (R-Ohio) unanimous consent request
quote.speaker: POLITICO

items.author: Matthew Zeitlin
items.title: The Bipartisan Buddies With a Plan to Fix Transmission
items.summary: Reps. Gabe Evans and Scott Peters released the CLEAR Act, which would apply to transmission lawsuits the stricter standards used for gas and hydropower projects. Peters expected a Senate package to include NEPA changes, limits on presidents canceling projects, and Section 401 reform.

quote.text: I think it’s coming together pretty well
quote.speaker: Rep. Scott Peters (D-Calif.)

items.title: Husted bill to protect Americans from footing the bill for new data centers blocked from passage
items.summary: Husted's account of the failed unanimous-consent request; says the bill would require state regulators to consider the standard.

quote.text: In plain language, if you create the cost, you should pay the cost.
quote.speaker: Sen. Jon Husted

items.author: Caitlin Yilek
items.title: Senate Democrat blocks House-passed bill to shield Americans from data center energy costs, proposing alternate measure
items.summary: Report on the Sept 17 floor exchange: Heinrich objects, offers GRID Savings Act, Moreno objects.

quote.text: Congress needs to pass real legislation with real teeth,
quote.speaker: Sen. Martin Heinrich

items.author: Josh Siegel
items.title: Permitting talks reach 'final' stages
items.summary: Capito said a deal was very close and Whitehouse said talks were in their final wrap-up, with the hardest issues resolved last. Capito conceded the floor vote could slip a week from the timeline she and Thune had set.

quote.text: in final wrap up, but some of the most difficult issues are the last ones resolved
quote.speaker: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.)

items.title: House passes ratepayer protection bill to limit data center cost shifts
items.summary: Covers House passage and notes critiques: the Center for Data Innovation wants one 100 MW standard for all large loads, and Heinrich says the House bill does not go far enough.

quote.text: Congress should apply the standard uniformly to any customer at 100 MW or more
quote.speaker: Michelle Lopes Maldonado, Center for Data Innovation

items.title: Congressman Gabe Evans' Bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act Passes the House
items.summary: Sponsor release on 417-3 passage, with quotes from Evans, Castor and Chairman Guthrie.

quote.text: My bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act ensures large data centers pay for the infrastructure they require while giving states the flexibility to determine what works best for their communities.
quote.speaker: Rep. Gabe Evans

items.author: Nicole Silverio
items.title: Major Permitting Bill Has Been Tied-Up In Senate For Months. What’s The Holdup?
items.summary: Reports the House-passed SPEED Act remains stalled in the Senate while environmental groups lobby against it and Republicans and business groups press for passage.

items.author: E&E News staff
items.title: Senators outline future of permitting talks
items.summary: After missing the August target, negotiators set September as the new deadline. Whitehouse wanted to avoid the lame duck and said the administration was 'not even close' on wind and solar. A federal judge in Oregon ordered the Pentagon to complete stalled onshore wind reviews. Environmental groups were wary, especially over how far to limit state Clean Water Act authority.

quote.text: There’s a major reset that they need to get to
quote.speaker: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.)

items.author: Lisa Martine Jenkins
items.title: One Senate Democrat's answer to Trump's 'ratepayer protection pledge'
items.summary: Compares the GRID Savings Act with H.R. 9340: the Senate bill is binding and FERC-run but covers transmission only and effectively skips ERCOT; the House bill covers generation, transmission and distribution and uses state commissions.

quote.text: The GRID Savings Act, should it become law, would reopen those sticky jurisdictional questions.
quote.speaker: Lisa Martine Jenkins, Latitude Media

items.title: Heinrich Introduces Legislation to Ensure Large Users of Electricity Pay for Grid Upgrades, Protect Customers From Costs of Data Center Expansion
items.summary: Sponsor release: applies to very large new electricity users the same basic approach long used for new power plants.

quote.text: If a company is driving the need for expensive new facilities, that company should pay for it — not families and small businesses.
quote.speaker: Sen. Martin Heinrich

items.author: Josh Siegel
items.title: Sen. Martin Heinrich on permitting reform, energy affordability and Trump's agenda
items.summary: POLITICO Energy's Josh Siegel interviews Sen. Heinrich, the top Democrat on Senate Energy and Natural Resources, on permitting reform, rising energy costs and the Trump agenda (about 21 minutes).

items.author: E&E News staff
items.title: Permitting deal may come after recess. Negotiators say that's OK.
items.summary: Heinrich said talks would likely run past the August recess and that the White House's attacks on renewables and its proposal to roll back tribal consultation under the historic preservation law made a deal harder. Schatz said a deal could come together in five days once the administration lifts its ban on clean energy. Whitehouse and Heinrich planned to meet Capito and Lee that week.

quote.text: I don’t think it’s too late
quote.speaker: Sen. Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.)

items.author: E&E News staff
items.title: Heinrich releases data center energy plan
items.summary: Heinrich previewed his GRID Savings Act, which would have FERC require large power users to pay for grid upgrades needed to connect. He said Democrats would make it a priority if he chairs the Energy Committee next year, and he opposed moratoria because they push data centers to places with the weakest rules.

quote.text: Pledges are great, but show me the reality.
quote.speaker: Sen. Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.)

items.author: Robinson Meyer
items.title: Meta Down, Permitting Odds Up
items.summary: Meyer lays out the six buckets of a likely deal (NEPA and judicial review, transmission, Clean Water Act, permit certainty, historic preservation, everything else) and says Lee's NHPA interest comes from his committee's jurisdiction. Prediction markets jumped to 77 percent that day.

quote.text: A permitting reform deal will probably have six buckets.
quote.speaker: Robinson Meyer, Heatmap

items.author: Jean Chemnick
items.title: EPA proposal could sideline the public on data center permits
items.summary: A July 1 EPA draft rule would drop federal requirements for public notice and comment when states permit minor pollution sources under Clean Air Act New Source Review. Advocates said it could let states permit data centers and power plants without telling nearby communities.

quote.text: EPA says it will empower states. Environmentalists say it will silence communities.
quote.speaker: E&E News

items.author: Michael Hoffman
items.title: Florida Rep. Byron Donalds pushes bill requiring AI data centers to supply their own power, water
items.summary: Local report on H.R. 9777, calling it a move past voluntary commitments.

quote.text: Donalds’ legislation would move beyond voluntary commitments by creating federal requirements for large-scale AI data centers.
quote.speaker: WFLX

items.author: Ryan McKeever, Emily Starobin, Sylvia Bartell, Michael Blackwell and Linda Walsh
items.title: RTOs and ISOs Answer: A National Preview of How All Six Grid Operators Plan to Respond to the Large Load Surge
items.summary: Law-firm summary of the six July 20 informational reports and what to expect in the August 17 show cause responses.

quote.text: The nation’s six regional grid operators recently told FERC how they plan to keep the lights on as large loads reshape the grid.
quote.speaker: Climate Solutions Legal Digest

items.title: President Trump Expands Historic Ratepayer Protection Pledge to Protect American Ratepayers, Lower Electricity Prices
items.summary: Announces the expansion and recaps the Pledge's five obligations.

quote.text: Today’s expansion includes governors, state legislators, developers, and power providers.
quote.speaker: EPA

items.author: Jason Plautz
items.title: Signed, sealed: Can Trump's ratepayer pledge deliver? (Power Switch)
items.summary: Twenty-three Republican governors and more than 200 utilities, co-ops, developers and state officials signed the nonbinding Ratepayer Protection Pledge. A law professor said what 'fair share' means is decided at the state utility regulator level.

quote.text: What ‘fair share’ looks like, when push comes to shove, gets answered at the state utility regulatory level.
quote.speaker: Cale Jaffe, University of Virginia law professor

items.author: Amelia Davidson
items.title: Data center lobby grumbles about reworked Ratepayer Protection Act
items.summary: The Data Center Coalition said it backed the original version and objected that the narrowed bill singles out data centers; steel and industrial energy consumer groups endorsed the change.

quote.text: the Energy & Commerce Committee’s changes to the bill narrow its scope to single out the data center industry
quote.speaker: Josh Levi, Data Center Coalition

items.author: Alec Stapp
items.title: Senate Republicans are interested in reforming the National Historic Preservation Act (NHPA)
items.summary: Alec Stapp of the Institute for Progress says Senate Republicans want National Historic Preservation Act reform in a permitting deal while Democrats are reluctant, and cites new research on how the reforms would affect clean energy versus fossil fuel projects.

items.author: Ethan Howland
items.title: FERC fails to shield PJM consumers from data center transmission costs: ratepayer advocates
items.summary: State ratepayer advocates say the PJM show cause order fails to address network upgrade cost allocation; RTOs had 60 days to respond, with possible 90-day extensions.

quote.text: Each network upgrade added to a transmission owner’s revenue requirement while these questions remain open embeds another cost shift
quote.speaker: State ratepayer advocates (Delaware, Illinois, Maryland, Ohio)

items.title: Trump-backed hopeful to succeed DeSantis unveils plan to protect local water, electricity from data centers
items.summary: Reports Donalds's bill would require data centers to get all electricity and water from private sources, and notes it is unclear whether the voluntary pledge is legally enforceable.

quote.text: But given the expected increase in demand, it’s unclear if the voluntary agreement is legally enforceable.
quote.speaker: Fortune

items.author: Amelia Davidson
items.title: House committee narrows data center energy bill
items.summary: Explains that committee leaders narrowed H.R. 9340 from any 100 MW load to data centers only, ahead of the markup.

quote.text: Previously, the bill language could be applied to projects with a peak electricity demand of 100 megawatts or more.
quote.speaker: E&E News

items.title: House Energy and Commerce Advances Energy Bills Aimed at Data Center Costs, Grid Modernization, and Pipeline Safety; Ratepayer Protection Act Clears 52-0
items.summary: Markup summary: the Evans substitute narrowed the definition to data centers; states keep authority over rate structures; members cite state large-load tariffs.

quote.text: An amendment in the nature of a substitute offered by Evans, which narrowed the definition of a large-load customer to data centers and hyperscalers above 100 megawatts of peak demand, was adopted by voice vote.
quote.speaker: Daily Energy Insider

items.author: Joel Kirkland
items.title: Can Congress get behind this data center bill? (Power Switch)
items.summary: After the 52-0 committee vote on the Ratepayer Protection Act, the newsletter notes the bill echoes a voluntary White House pledge and has a shot in the Senate, though Mike Lee had called data center legislation not a priority. It also reports Sen. David McCormick in line to chair the Energy Committee next Congress.

quote.text: Energy and Natural Resources Chair Mike Lee (R-Utah) has said data center legislation is not currently a “priority”
quote.speaker: POLITICO Power Switch

items.title: Husted leads bill to protect Americans from footing the bill for new data centers
items.summary: Sponsor release: the bill would codify key elements of the White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge and sets a 100 MW threshold.

quote.text: The Ratepayer Protection Act would codify key elements of that pledge.
quote.speaker: Sen. Jon Husted

items.author: Josh Siegel
items.title: Permitting deal deadline remains elusive
items.summary: The August recess goal for a deal was slipping. Democratic negotiators were pressing for transmission measures and limits on the administration's power to cancel approved projects; King said the administration had to take its thumb off the scale.

quote.text: until the administration takes their thumb off the scale, we’re not going to be able to do it
quote.speaker: Sen. Angus King (I-Maine)

items.author: Nico Portuondo
items.title: New England gas crunch puts Sheldon Whitehouse in a bind
items.summary: High power prices and offshore wind delays had New England Democrats split on new gas pipelines. Whitehouse, a lead permitting negotiator, said the pipeline question needed consideration.

quote.text: the pipeline question requires some consideration
quote.speaker: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.)

items.author: Robinson Meyer
items.title: Scoop: A Key Democrat Wants to Break America's Worst Energy Bottleneck
items.summary: Heinrich introduced a bill letting new power plants of any type skip full interconnection studies in exchange for curtailing output when the grid is congested, copying the Texas approach. Heatmap saw it as the kind of technology-neutral bill that could slot into a permitting package.

quote.text: would make it easier for new power plants to hook up to electricity markets across the country
quote.speaker: Heatmap (Robinson Meyer)

items.author: Jane Flegal
items.title: Let me just say, if Democrats reject a permitting deal with a robust transmission provision
items.summary: Responding to a Siegel report that NHPA is the main sticking point between negotiators, Flegal says she would be disappointed if Democrats reject a deal with strong transmission provisions over NHPA concerns.

quote.text: if Democrats reject a permitting deal with a robust transmission provision because of NHPA angst, I will be very, very disappointed.
quote.speaker: Jane Flegal

items.author: Josh Siegel
items.title: Where the permitting talks stand
items.summary: Negotiators agreed on the broad contours but were haggling over details. A Democrat close to the talks said Republicans made a broad offer before the July Fourth recess covering faster environmental and historic preservation reviews, some transmission permitting and GOP priorities. Democrats wanted stronger transmission and limits on the president's power to cancel permits, and advocates worried the vote would slip to the lame duck.

quote.text: The window of opportunity there is starting to close this Congress
quote.speaker: Jason Grumet, American Clean Power Association

items.author: Sarah Wang and Tyler Farrell
items.title: Understanding FERC's Large Load Orders
items.summary: Summary of FERC's six June orders, their deadlines, and the five reform categories.

quote.text: FERC’s show cause orders apply only to RTOs
quote.speaker: RMI

items.author: Miranda Willson
items.title: Groups urge lawmakers to protect state water reviews in permitting talks
items.summary: Nearly 60 national and regional groups wrote to the Senate EPW Committee against limiting state and tribal Section 401 water reviews. Republicans and the administration say blue states have used Section 401 to slow or block energy projects.

quote.text: Environmental advocates are pushing back on a top Republican priority in ongoing energy permitting reform negotiations.
quote.speaker: E&E News (Miranda Willson)

items.author: E&E News staff
items.title: Data center energy bill hits speed bump
items.summary: Frank Pallone's call for a national data center moratorium overshadowed the Energy and Commerce vote on the Ratepayer Protection Act. The bill would require states to consider a federal cost standard that state regulators could reject. Google, Microsoft and the Data Center Coalition backed it; environmental groups opposed it.

quote.text: we need action, not toothless promises from Big Tech
quote.speaker: Rep. Frank Pallone (D-N.J.)

items.author: E&E News staff
items.title: EPA floats changes to NEPA implementation rules
items.summary: EPA proposed changes to its NEPA procedures to follow the 2023 Fiscal Responsibility Act (two-year, 150-page limits for impact statements), the One Big Beautiful Bill Act fee for faster reviews, and last year's Supreme Court ruling that narrowed the scope of review. CEQ data cited: final impact statements took 2.8 years and 661 pages on average.

quote.text: In recent years, final EISs took an average of 2.8 years to complete while clocking in at an average of 661 pages, according to CEQ reviews.
quote.speaker: E&E News

items.author: Matthew Zeitlin
items.title: The Mystery of the Ratepayer Protection Act
items.summary: Explains why hyperscalers back the bill. Harvard's Ari Peskoe calls its PURPA standard largely symbolic because Congress cannot force state regulators to act.

quote.text: largely symbolic
quote.speaker: Ari Peskoe, Harvard Law School

items.author: Ethan Howland
items.title: 6 takeaways from FERC's data center interconnection decision
items.summary: Explains the six show cause orders, the five reform areas, the regional approach, and that FERC avoided state retail jurisdiction.

quote.text: Nothing in this order is intended to intrude upon state authority over retail service to large loads.
quote.speaker: FERC (PJM show cause order)

items.author: Robinson Meyer
items.title: 'We Proved That America Can Still Build Big Things' (Heinrich on SunZia)
items.summary: In an interview marking SunZia's completion, Heinrich said he was working to get to yes and that transmission is an essential piece of a balanced package that could reach 65 or 70 votes.

quote.text: We have to make sure that it’s an effectively balanced package — that’s how you get to 65, 70 votes.
quote.speaker: Sen. Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.)

items.author: Matthew Zeitlin
items.title: FERC Has a New Plan for Data Centers
items.summary: FERC voted 5-0 to send show cause orders to six grid operators, covering study rules, cost-shift safeguards, co-location, flexible service and proximate generation. FERC chose region-by-region orders over a national rule.

quote.text: If new infrastructure is built to accommodate a data center, and that data center doesn’t show up, residential customers are not left on the hook to pay the costs
quote.speaker: FERC Commissioner David Rosner

items.author: Josh Siegel
items.title: Senate releases NDAA with permitting amendment
items.summary: The Senate Armed Services Committee released its fiscal 2027 defense bill with an amendment by Sen. Angus King to curb the Pentagon's delay in processing wind project permits. Chair Roger Wicker said the dispute needed to be resolved.

quote.text: It needs to be resolved and there’s bipartisan support for that
quote.speaker: Sen. Roger Wicker (R-Miss.)

items.author: Robinson Meyer
items.title: Freedom (It Won't Slow You Down)
items.summary: Cortez Masto and Cotton released a Senate version of the FREEDOM Act that keeps future presidents from interfering with permitted projects. It dropped the House bill's de-risking compensation program and lets a court appoint a contractor to finish a stalled permit. Heatmap calls such a provision essential to any deal.

quote.text: Most importantly, it jettisons a de-risking compensation program.
quote.speaker: Heatmap (Robinson Meyer)

items.author: Emily Yehle
items.title: Special edition: POLITICO's Energy Summit kicks off hot permitting summer (Power Switch)
items.summary: At POLITICO's Energy Summit, Capito and Whitehouse both urged the White House to stop attacking renewables, and White House energy council director Jarrod Agen blamed Democrats for opposing gas pipelines and called New York's water-permit review the kind of rule permitting reform would fix. FERC's Swett said a data center cost action was days away.

quote.text: The governor of New York is using regulation to stop a pipeline — using a water regulation that we’re trying to fix in this permitting reform
quote.speaker: Jarrod Agen, White House National Energy Dominance Council

items.author: Josh Siegel
items.title: Debate over preservation law tripping up permitting talks
items.summary: Mike Lee's push to change the National Historic Preservation Act had become a major sticking point. Lee wanted limits on lawsuits; some Democrats were wary because the law matters to tribes and preservation groups. Heinrich said the aim was to preserve the law's intent while making reviews more predictable.

quote.text: how do you find that balance of where you preserve the intent, but make things more predictable and efficient?
quote.speaker: Sen. Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.)

items.author: Jael Holzman
items.title: How Has the Rise of AI Changed the Odds of a Permitting Deal? (Q&A with ACORE's Ray Long)
items.summary: ACORE's Ray Long says data center load is a catalyst for permitting reform. He cites 166 gigawatts of needed power over four years, about half for data centers, and says a bill would have to come from a Senate deal in an election year.

quote.text: The data center load is a part of the catalyst to get people talking about it
quote.speaker: Ray Long, ACORE

items.outlet: Center for Climate and Energy Solutions
items.title: Federal Permitting Reform in the 119th Congress: Comparing the CERTAIN, FREEDOM, and SPEED Acts
items.summary: C2ES compares three House permitting bills in the 119th Congress: the CERTAIN Act, the FREEDOM Act and the SPEED Act.

items.author: Alex Music
items.title: Bipartisan drive for permitting reform grows, but outlook is still murky
items.summary: Reports Republicans and Democrats share ground on permitting certainty while recent Trump administration moves impede negotiations.

items.author: E&E News staff
items.title: Wright meets with Republicans on permitting, but deal remains elusive as ever
items.summary: After a dinner of the four Senate committee leaders and a separate Wright dinner with Republicans, E&E reported broad support for a deal but no clear path. Heinrich said the administration's stalled solar, wind and battery permits were the biggest threat. Whitehouse said Democrats would hold a caucus vote before moving any bill.

quote.text: The thing that is the biggest threat to permitting reform right now is that the Trump administration backslid into a series of stalled-out permits
quote.speaker: Sen. Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.)

items.title: 73 western groups to Senate leadership: No deal with devil on permit reform
items.summary: Seventy-three western community, conservation, faith and Indigenous groups send a joint letter to Schumer, Heinrich, Whitehouse and Jeffries urging them to reconsider pursuing permitting legislation under the current Congress and administration.

quote.text: The first rule of negotiation is that it’s impossible to reach workable solutions with bad-faith actors
quote.speaker: Erik Schlenker-Goodrich, Western Environmental Law Center

items.author: Hannah Story Brown
items.title: NEPA and Its Discontents
items.summary: Magazine feature on how NEPA has been rewritten by the last three administrations and what it says is missing from the political debate over permitting reform, including the SPEED Act's limits on the law.

quote.text: It would be more honest for them to just say they want to repeal NEPA, because the SPEED Act constrains it so much
quote.speaker: Ana Unruh Cohen, former Biden administration NEPA official

items.author: E&E News staff
items.title: Permitting talks live on as DOJ declines to appeal ruling favoring Revolution Wind
items.summary: The administration let the deadline pass without appealing a ruling that blocked the Interior stop-work order on Revolution Wind. Whitehouse had threatened to pause talks again if the administration kept attacking renewables and said an appeal would be inconsistent with progress.

quote.text: We are watching those and would view any appeal as inconsistent with further progress on permitting reform
quote.speaker: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.)

items.title: Heinrich and Whitehouse Joint Statement on Permitting Reform
items.summary: Sens. Heinrich and Whitehouse say permitting talks are resuming, conditioned on the administration continuing to approve renewable energy permits.

quote.text: Seeing permits continuing to be approved by the administration is critical for ensuring that talks can continue.
quote.speaker: Sens. Martin Heinrich and Sheldon Whitehouse

items.title: Ratepayer Protection Pledge
items.summary: Five voluntary commitments by signers: new power supply, paying for delivery upgrades, paying whether or not they use the power, local workforce, and grid resilience.

quote.text: Companies will voluntarily negotiate new, separate rate structures with their utilities and relevant State governments wherever they build data centers.
quote.speaker: White House

items.author: Hodan Omaar

items.summary: Think-tank critique: the GRID Act's credits and penalties single out data centers instead of reforming how markets handle large loads. Its summary of the DOE study and credits is the author's reading of the bill.

quote.text: the GRID Act imposes a punitive tax-and-subsidize regime exclusively for data centers
quote.speaker: Hodan Omaar, ITIF

quote.text: It does not mandate that agencies choose environmentally friendly alternatives or prohibit projects with significant impacts.
quote.speaker: Ben Schifman, Institute for Progress

items.author: Amelia Davidson
items.title: Bipartisan bill would force data centers to find own power sources
items.summary: News report on the GRID Act; calls it the first bipartisan proposal to keep data centers from raising consumer energy costs.

quote.text: is the first bipartisan proposal intended to stop the artificial intelligence infrastructure from increasing energy costs for consumers
quote.speaker: E&E News

items.title: Hawley, Blumenthal Introduce Bill to Prevent Data Centers from Increasing Electricity Costs for Americans
items.summary: Sponsor release with a bullet summary of the GRID Act.

quote.text: Senator Hawley’s new bill would require data centers to have their own power sources, ensuring that the costs of their business are not passed on to American consumers.
quote.speaker: Sen. Josh Hawley release

items.author: Robinson Meyer
items.title: What Senator Martin Heinrich Needs to See in a Permitting Deal
items.summary: Robinson Meyer interviews Sen. Heinrich on the state of play on permitting reform, what a bipartisan energy deal would need to do on transmission, and lessons from passing and partly repealing the Inflation Reduction Act.

items.author: Alexander C. Kaufman
items.title: Scoop: New Bipartisan House Bill Would Keep President From Yanking Permits
items.summary: Reps. Harder, Gray, Lawler, Bacon and Edwards introduced the FREEDOM Act, a 77-page bill barring agencies from halting fully permitted projects and creating a compensation fund. quote.text: The FREEDOM Act delivers the smart, pro-growth certainty that critical energy projects desperately need by cutting delays, fast-tracking approvals, and holding federal agencies accountable
quote.speaker: Rep. Josh Harder (D-Calif.)

items.author: Ethan Howland
items.title: Republican, Democratic senators call for project certainty at permitting reform hearing
items.summary: Reports on the Jan. 28 EPW hearing, where senators of both parties backed reform but Whitehouse said progress depends on the administration ending its moves against wind and solar projects.

quote.speaker: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse

items.outlet: YouTube / Senate Environment & Public Works Committee
items.title: Trump’s lawlessness halts permitting reform in the Senate. No certainty, no reform.
items.summary: Full-committee EPW hearing on bipartisan permitting reform (about 2 hours), uploaded by the committee's Democratic channel under a title that criticizes the administration's blockade of clean energy projects.

items.outlet: LIUNA (Laborers’ International Union of North America)
items.author: Brent Booker
items.title: Move Infrastructure, Good Jobs and the Nation Forward By Getting Politics and Needless Delays Out of Permitting, Leader of Largest Union of Construction Laborers Tells Senate Committee
items.summary: LIUNA's general president testifies at the Jan. 28 EPW hearing in favor of bipartisan permitting reform, citing court delays and the politics of permit cancellations as threats to project certainty.

quote.text: Today the greatest threat to project certainty is not litigation alone, it is the politics being played with our members’ jobs
quote.speaker: Brent Booker, LIUNA General President

items.author: Sheldon Whitehouse
items.title: Whitehouse Opening Statement at Permitting Reform Hearing
items.summary: Whitehouse's opening statement at the Jan. 28 EPW hearing says he wants strong bipartisan permitting reform but that a trust problem with the administration's behavior must be solved first.

quote.text: The responsibility for resuscitating permitting reform rests now upon the executive branch, upon credible confidence that the nonsense will stop
quote.speaker: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse

items.author: Shelley Moore Capito
items.title: Chairman Capito Opening Statement at Hearing to Examine Federal Permitting Processes
items.summary: Capito's opening statement for the Jan. 28 EPW hearing on federal environmental review and permitting, calling for bipartisan reforms that make permitting more predictable.

quote.text: remove the politics from permitting once and for all.
quote.speaker: Sen. Shelley Moore Capito

items.title: CEQ Finalizes Rescission of NEPA Implementing Regulations
items.summary: Law firm client alert on CEQ's January 2026 final rule rescinding its NEPA regulations, saying agency-specific NEPA procedures now serve as the primary operational framework.

items.title: Van Hollen Leads New Bill to Ensure Americans Aren't Footing the Bill for Big Data Centers
items.summary: Sponsor release with PJM cost figures and a list of supporting consumer groups.

quote.text: the huge corporations building and running data centers should cover the costs of the energy they need – not push those costs onto the backs of consumers
quote.speaker: Sen. Chris Van Hollen

items.author: Lee Zeldin
items.title: EPA Proposes CWA Section 401 Rule to Streamline Permitting, Unleash Economic Growth, and Protect America’s Waterways
items.summary: EPA proposes a Clean Water Act Section 401 rule it says would stop states from using water quality certification to block infrastructure for unrelated reasons; the release carries supportive statements from Sen. Capito and Rep. Graves.

items.title: Removal of National Environmental Policy Act Implementing Regulations
items.summary: CEQ's final rule (91 FR 618) adopts without changes its February 2025 interim final rule that removed the agency's NEPA implementing regulations from the Code of Federal Regulations.

items.author: White House CEQ
items.title: NEWS: CEQ Fixes Decades-Long Permitting Failure Through Deregulation Today, CEQ affirmed the removal
items.summary: The Council on Environmental Quality's account announces a final rule affirming removal of the agency's NEPA implementing regulations.

items.title: CEQ Fixes Decades-Long Permitting Failure Through Deregulation
items.summary: The White House announces CEQ has finalized the removal of its NEPA implementing regulations, completing the administration's effort to rescind the rules.

quote.text: NEPA’s regulatory reign of terror has ended
quote.speaker: Katherine Scarlett, CEQ Chairman

items.author: Ethan Howland
items.title: Senate Democrats end permitting reform talks over offshore wind freeze
items.summary: Reports that Sens. Whitehouse and Heinrich ended permitting negotiations after the Trump administration halted work on five offshore wind projects totaling about 7 GW.

quote.text: The illegal attacks on fully permitted renewable energy projects must be reversed if there is to be any chance that permitting talks resume
quote.speaker: Sens. Sheldon Whitehouse and Martin Heinrich

items.author: Marcel Akhame, Daniel Elizalde and Xan Fishman
items.title: What’s in the SPEED Act?
items.summary: BPC issue brief, updated for the House-passed text, explaining the SPEED Act's changes to NEPA procedures and judicial review.

quote.text: The SPEED Act marks the first major bipartisan permitting reform proposal in the 119th Congress.
quote.speaker: Bipartisan Policy Center

items.author: Earthjustice Action
items.title: "The SPEED Act will only result in an abundance of contaminated air and water, dirty projects
items.summary: Earthjustice Action quotes opposition to the SPEED Act after House passage, saying it would mean more pollution and fewer chances to hold polluters accountable in court, and links AP coverage.

items.author: Joshua Siegel
items.title: SPEED story: House passes major GOP-led permitting overhaul after late drama.
items.summary: Siegel posts his report on the House passing the SPEED Act and sending permitting legislation to the Senate.

items.author: Bruce Westerman
items.title: House Passes Historic Bipartisan Permitting Reform Legislation
items.summary: The committee announces House passage of H.R. 4776, the SPEED Act, which it says modernizes NEPA to shorten reviews and curb litigation delays.

quote.text: The passage of the SPEED Act is a win for America.
quote.speaker: Rep. Bruce Westerman, committee chairman

items.author: Emily Pontecorvo
items.title: The House Just Passed Permitting Reform. Now Comes the Hard Part.
items.summary: The House passed the SPEED Act 221-196 after a late change that exempted agency actions between Jan. 20 and enactment from the bill's anti-revocation language. ACP withdrew its support; Huffman said it was going nowhere in the Senate; Rep. Adam Gray voted yes expecting the Senate to fix it.

quote.text: Even if the House passes this bill today, it is going nowhere in the Senate
quote.speaker: Rep. Jared Huffman (D-Calif.)

items.author: Drew Maloney
items.title: EEI Statement on House Passage of the SPEED Act
items.summary: EEI's president and CEO calls House passage of the SPEED Act an important first step toward cutting red tape and lowering customer costs, and says EEI will keep working on a more predictable and durable permitting system for all energy forms.

quote.text: The House passage of the Speed Act is an important first step toward cutting red tape, lowering customer costs, and delivering reliable, affordable electricity to American families and businesses.
quote.speaker: Drew Maloney, EEI President and CEO

items.author: Kelsey Brugger and Amelia Davidson
items.title: House approves permitting bill after tumultuous week
items.summary: Reports the House passed the SPEED Act 221-196 with 11 Democrats in support, with Westerman and Huffman offering opposing views of the bill on the floor.

items.author: Emily Pontecorvo
items.title: The House passed the SPEED Act today, which would make sweeping changes to NEPA.
items.summary: Heatmap reporter Emily Pontecorvo notes the House passed the SPEED Act, that a last-minute tweak on previously approved renewable projects angered many, and that a Senate deal will not be easy.

items.author: Kelsey Brugger
items.title: How Republicans saved the ‘SPEED Act’ from oblivion
items.summary: Reports House leaders agreed to amend the SPEED Act to win over offshore wind opponents who had threatened to block floor debate.

items.author: Jael Holzman
items.title: Exclusive: Key Senate Democrats Oppose Permitting Bill
items.summary: Reports that Sens. Heinrich, Whitehouse and Schatz came out against passing the House SPEED Act, citing how it would apply to renewable energy and transmission.

quote.text: We are committed to streamlining the permitting process — but only if it ensures we can build out transmission and cheap, clean energy.
quote.speaker: Sens. Heinrich, Whitehouse and Schatz, joint statement

items.author: Emily Pontecorvo
items.title: Permitting Reform is Back. What Are We Even Talking About This Time?
items.summary: A guide to the SPEED Act: it would cut the NEPA suit window from up to six years to 150 days, limit suits to people who commented, and set court timelines. Heatmap says Democrats would not agree to a deal that does not bar the president from pulling approved permits.

quote.text: Democrats have said they won’t agree to a deal that doesn’t bar the president from pulling previously-approved permits or otherwise level the playing field for renewable energy.
quote.speaker: Heatmap (Emily Pontecorvo)

items.author: Joshua Siegel
items.title: Key Senate Dems are laying out their demands as House takes up permitting.
items.summary: Siegel reports Sen. Schatz says any bipartisan reform should address Trump's attacks on clean energy, including canceled or stalled projects, and should include transmission action.

quote.text: truly address Trump’s attacks on clean energy
quote.speaker: Sen. Brian Schatz, as quoted by Joshua Siegel

items.author: Jael Holzman
items.title: Trump Is the Biggest Wild Card in Permitting Reform
items.summary: After the House Natural Resources vote of 25-18, Holzman reports that Democrats in both chambers would not back a deal without limits on the president's power over wind and solar permits. Reps. Levin and Casten proposed a parity rule between fossil and non-fossil projects; Golden's no-rescission language was added in committee.

quote.text: Any deal hinges on the Trump administration providing assurances they’re not going to kill every single clean energy project in existence
quote.speaker: Rep. Mike Levin (D-Calif.)

items.outlet: Center for Climate and Energy Solutions (YouTube)
items.title: Keeping the Lights On: Can permitting reform unlock affordable, reliable energy?
items.summary: C2ES event (about 70 minutes) on permitting reform proposals before the 119th Congress and their implications for the power sector.

items.title: Environmental Groups Speak Out Against Deregulatory SPEED Act
items.summary: WE ACT publishes statements from environmental and community organizations opposing H.R. 4776, the SPEED Act, saying it would limit environmental review and public input and speed approval of fossil fuel projects.

quote.text: The SPEED Act would do the opposite, adding more dangerous fossil fuel projects to the backyards of communities
quote.speaker: WE ACT for Environmental Justice

items.author: Jason Grumet
items.title: ACP Statement on House Natural Resources Committee Advancing Permitting Bill
items.summary: ACP's CEO welcomes the 25-18 House Natural Resources Committee vote advancing the SPEED Act, citing its milestones and technology neutrality.

quote.text: Today’s bipartisan action in the House Natural Resources Committee is an essential step toward modernizing American energy infrastructure.
quote.speaker: Jason Grumet, ACP CEO

items.author: Elizabeth McCarthy
items.title: The Fall of Permitting Reform
items.summary: Breakthrough Institute analysis of why permitting reform has stalled despite broad agreement, citing Democratic wariness of NEPA changes and jurisdiction split across two House and two Senate committees.

quote.text: No chair can carry a comprehensive deal alone.
quote.speaker: Elizabeth McCarthy, Breakthrough Institute

items.author: E&E News staff
items.title: Whitehouse threatens to blow up permitting talks
items.summary: At an EPW hearing Whitehouse said it made little sense to pursue bipartisan permitting reform while the administration would not faithfully execute the law, citing the Revolution Wind stop-work order and canceled solar approvals. He even threatened to oppose routine water and highway bills.

quote.text: Why would we want to do bipartisan permitting reform during an administration that won’t faithfully execute that law?
quote.speaker: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.)

items.author: Rachel Levine
items.title: Permitting reform is back, and here’s how Congress can get it done this time
items.summary: Niskanen argues Congress could pass a package combining support for clean-firm generation, common-sense NEPA updates and faster approval of major transmission lines, citing demand growth from AI.

items.author: Sammie Firth
items.title: Rolling back NEPA puts clean energy progress—and public trust—at risk
items.summary: CATF argues that agencies' new NEPA procedures, issued largely as nonbinding guidance after CEQ rescinded its regulations, limit public engagement and create uncertainty for clean energy projects.

items.title: Shelley Moore Capito And Sheldon Whitehouse Urge Support For Federal Permitting Reform
items.summary: Senate floor remarks in which Sens. Capito and Whitehouse speak in support of permitting reform, posted by Forbes Breaking News.

items.author: Doug Burgum
items.title: Department of the Interior Curbs Preferential Treatment for Wind Energy
items.summary: Interior announces policy measures, including Secretary's Order 3437, to end what it calls preferential treatment for wind and solar in departmental decision-making and to review offshore wind rules.

quote.text: These policy changes represent a commonsense approach to energy that puts Americans’ interests first
quote.speaker: Doug Burgum, Interior Secretary

items.title: Earthjustice Statement on Westerman-Golden Permitting Reform Bill
items.summary: Earthjustice opposes the newly introduced SPEED Act, saying it would further the administration's fossil fuel push and bring more pollution and dirty air and water.

quote.text: This proposal will only result in more pollution, poorer health outcomes, and dirty air and water for everyone.
quote.speaker: Earthjustice

items.author: Chris Wright
items.title: Energy Secretary Announces Updated NEPA Procedures to End Permitting Paralysis and Unleash American Energy
items.summary: DOE announces updated NEPA procedures that it says cut red tape, with firm review deadlines and page limits for environmental reviews.

quote.text: America can and will build big things again, but we must cut the red tape that has brought American energy innovation to a standstill
quote.speaker: Chris Wright, Energy Secretary

items.author: Robinson Meyer and Jesse D. Jenkins
items.title: The Supreme Court’s Double-Edged Change to Permitting Law
items.summary: Hosts Robinson Meyer and Jesse Jenkins discuss Justice Kavanaugh's NEPA opinion in the Seven County case with University of Michigan law professor Nicholas Bagley.

items.outlet: Supreme Court of the United States (via Cornell LII)
items.title: SEVEN COUNTY INFRASTRUCTURE COALITION v. EAGLE COUNTY
items.summary: The Court's 8-0 opinion by Justice Kavanaugh reversing the D.C. Circuit, holding that courts must give agencies substantial deference in NEPA cases and that NEPA review need not cover effects of separate upstream or downstream projects.

quote.text: The D. C. Circuit failed to afford the Board the substantial judicial deference required in NEPA cases
quote.speaker: Supreme Court syllabus
